message.reasoning_content:
Analyze the kernel: uses stable formulation: for x<0, sigmoid = exp(-|x|)/(1+exp(-|x|)) = exp(x)/(1+exp(x)); for x>=0, 1/(1+exp(-x)). Both branches use FP32 exp and div_rn, then cvt.rn.f16.f32. Contract: correctly-rounded-once FP16. FP32 intermediate (exp accurate to ~1ulp, division exact rounding) then a single FP16 round — may double-round incorrectly for values near FP16 rounding boundaries. Also FP32 computation error ~1ulp could flip ties. Risk: double rounding and exp accuracy. Also signed zero: for x=+0, x<0 false → 1/(1+1)=0.5 fine. For x negative large, exp(-|x|) tiny → numerator tiny, denominator ~1 → tiny positive → cvt to subnormal or zero. cvt.rn.f16.f32 handles subnormals and flush? f16 conversions in PTX by default may flush subnormals? cvt.rn.f16.f32 supports subnormals unless .ftz specified — no ftz here, so fine.
